newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed to lower, await Wall St.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed to lower, await Wall St.

text.p: U.S. shares were mixed to lower in Europe on Friday as some investors feared Thursday's sell-off on Wall Street could herald a deeper downside correction in the near-term, dealers said.
"There are a few people talking the market down this morning," one market maker said. "Some are saying we may be at the start of the long-awaited pull-back."
"But we've had so many false alarms since last summer that it's a brave man who believes this is the beginning of the end."
In New York on Thursday, the Dow plunged 94.28 points or 1.38 percent to close at 6,755.75.
IBM, which dropped $5-5/8, or 3.6 percent, on Thursday after losing $12 on Wednesday, was off $1/4 at $151-1/2 versus a U.S. close of $151-3/4.
Other high-technology issues were lower, with Intel down $1/4 at $151-1/2, Texas Instruments down $1/4 at $70-3/4, and Compaq $1/8 easier at $83-5/8.
General Motors was up $3/8 at $62-3/8 after the Wall Street Journal reported that the automaker could raise its dividend and begin a huge stock repurchase plan Monday.
PepsiCo, which confirmed on Thursday plans to spin off its restaurant division, was up $5/8 at $34-7/8.
Dealers here expect the Dow to start lower with the S&P 500 futures contract on Globex down 2.15 points at 778.15 by 1110 GMT.
The March T-bond was off 7/32 at 110-20/32.
"A bit of consolidation would not be a surprise after such a good run," another dealer said.
So far in 1997, the Dow has risen 307.48 points, or 4.77 percent and the broader S&P-500 36.82 points, or 4.97 percent, as of Thursday's close.
